newsitem.title: FINLAND: HUHTAMAKI, HERSHEY TO SWAP ASSETS.
newsitem.headline: HUHTAMAKI, HERSHEY TO SWAP ASSETS.

text.p: Finnish confectionery and packaging group Huhtamaki Oy said on Friday it planned to sell its Leaf North America confectionery operations and license its brands to U.S. confectionery group Hershey Foods.
Huhtamaki will also buy Hershey's European confectionery interests, it said in a statement.

"This will have a significant positive impact on our profitability next year," Huhtamaki CEO Timo Peltola told a news conference. The deal would reduce Huhtamaki's annual net sales by about one billion markka, he said.

"Huhtamaki ... and Hershey Foods ... have reached a preliminary agreement on brand licensing and (an) asset swap involving their North American and European confectionery interests," Huhtamaki said in a statement.
Hershey will pay $440 million for the North American confectionery operations, the statement said.
Huhtamaki will pay $110 million for Hershey's European confectionery interests, the German praline maker Gubor Schokoladen and the Italian sugar confectionery company Sperlari.
The deal, which is subject to regulatory approval, is due to be completed by year-end, Huhtamaki said.
"Huhtamaki will retain the ownership of Leaf's North American trademarks and will receive an annual royalty on Hershey's sales of these brands," it said.
Leaf's North American confectionery net sales in 1995 were about $460 million, while Gubor and Sperlari had combined sales of about $210 million.
Huhtamaki said the deal had been motivated by shareholder interest.
"Leaf's profitability in North America has been lower than in Europe. The same was true for Hershey's European business, compared to their North American levels," Peltola said in the statement.
It would allow Huhtamaki to concentrate on building Leaf's European and Asian businesses, the company added.
It quoted Hershey CEO and chairman Kenneth Wolfe as saying the deal would allow each company to focus on its core markets.

"The consolidation of Leaf's North American confectionery operations into our current business will allow us to leverage our existing capabilities, to create synergies and to better serve both customers and consumers."
